subtopic: Buying and Redeeming Money Market Fund Shares
source_evidence: investors can generally sell their shares back to a money market fund on any business day at the net asset value (NAV) per share.
answer: Buying and redeeming money market fund shares works much like it does for other mutual funds: you buy shares from the fund itself or through a broker for the fund, rather than from another investor on a national securities market. Shares are generally redeemable on demand, so you can usually sell them back to the fund on any business day at the fund’s net asset value (NAV) per share. Many funds intended for retail investors and government money market funds seek to keep a stable NAV of $1.00 per share. By contrast, institutional prime and institutional tax-exempt funds have a floating NAV, so their share price may be more or less than $1.00.
